entry.title: Environment · Mon, Nov 2, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: Western Virginia Water Authority Water Supply Study Results Briefing. City Council's informal session agenda scheduled a 30-minute briefing on the results of the Western Virginia Water Authority water supply study.
Proposed: Erosion and Stormwater Management Code Update Community Meeting Announcement. The consent agenda included a community meeting announcement scheduled for November 19, 2026, to collect public comment on proposed draft updates to City Code Chapter 11.8 concerning Erosion and Stormwater Management.

entry.title: Environment · Mon, Jul 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: City Manager Comments on Belmont Library Environmental Camp and Tinker Creek Cleanup. The City Manager provided updates on Belmont Branch Library's Environmental Camp and the upcoming 10th annual Tinker Creek Cleanup hosted by the Stormwater Division.
Adopted: Amended Intergovernmental Agreement for Roanoke Valley Greenway. The City Council adopted an ordinance approving an Amended and Restated Intergovernmental Agreement regarding the Roanoke Valley Greenway. Recorded vote: 7-0.

entry.title: Environment · Mon, Jul 6, 2026
entry.summary:
Adopted: Project Outside Grant for Brushy Mountain. Council adopted an ordinance accepting and appropriating a Project Outside Grant for Brushy Mountain. Recorded vote: 7-0.
Discussion / report: Water Matters to Roanoke Conservation Campaign. The City Manager announced the launch of the 'Water Matters to Roanoke' conservation campaign in coordination with the Western Virginia Water Authority to raise awareness about water resources and the Drought Contingency Plan.
Official source: https://roanokeva.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=6513,plainText=false)

entry.title: Environment · Mon, Jun 15, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: Follow-Up on Evans Spring Preservation Concerns. The Inclusive Services Manager reported that Community Engagement reached out to two residents who voiced concerns on May 18 regarding Evans Spring preservation and zoning text amendments, but neither resident responded.
Discussion / report: Drought Conditions and Water Conservation Measures. Council members and the Mayor discussed potential messaging and triggers for voluntary versus mandatory water conservation measures in response to drought conditions, noting Western Virginia Water Authority's role.
Official source: https://roanokeva.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=6502,plainText=false)

entry.title: Environment · Mon, Jun 1, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: CeeBreeze Property Tree Canopy Restoration Update. The City Manager reported that the New River Conservancy completed the planting of approximately 175 trees, shrubs, and native plants to restore tree canopy at the former CeeBreeze property on Syracuse Avenue NW, with staff incorporating provided soil amendments, compost, and biochar.
Official source: https://roanokeva.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=6491,plainText=false)

entry.title: Environment · Mon, May 4, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: Discussion on Water Quality Focus Group. Vice-Mayor McGuire reported on discussions with a Franklin County Supervisor regarding resuscitating an inter-jurisdictional focus group on water quality and health.
Discussion / report: Discussion and Withdrawal of Council Member Initiative on Solarization. Vice-Mayor McGuire announced he would not move forward with a Council Member Initiative on solarization, discussing potential federal savings under the Inflation Reduction Act and the Climate Action Plan. Mayor Cobb said staff were weighing credits and upfront costs as a potential capital-improvement budget matter.
Official source: https://roanokeva.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=6465,plainText=false)

entry.title: Environment · Mon, Oct 5, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: Stormwater Annual Compliance Report. The City Manager highlighted the completion of the City's annual stormwater compliance report, noting accomplishments such as 10 citywide street-sweeping cycles removing over 1,000 tons of sediment, storm drain cleanings, inspections of nearly 29,000 feet of pipe, and outreach to more than 38,000 residents.
Official source: https://roanokeva.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=6579,plainText=false)
